title: Start and exit points: Waterjet Profile (pierce point and jet-off point)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Refs #1448. Follow-up of #3334.

## What happens

Waterjet Profile is on `main` now. It does not take a start pick or an exit pick. `KindInfo::pick()` answers `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` for `OpType::WaterjetProfile` (`crates/app/src/operation/pick_kinds.rs`). A pick on a waterjet operation is refused by name. The user cannot set the pierce point or the place where the jet goes off.

#3334 gave the rule for this kind: "A waterjet kind that `main` adds later takes the same pick through the shared mechanism." The plasma slice of #3334 did not include the waterjet planner.

## Expected

- Start: the pierce is at the lead-in start that lands on the projection of the start pick on the profile.
- Exit: the lead-out and the jet off are at the projection of the exit pick.
- The picks are the operation-level `picks` (#3339). MCP `edit_operation` sets them.

Seam: `crates/motion/src/waterjet/plan.rs` (the seam is `longest_mid`). The plasma slice is the pattern: `crates/motion/src/plasma/picks.rs` (`assign`, `run_on`) and `plan_closed` in `crates/motion/src/plasma/emit.rs`. The pick assignment can move to `crates/motion/src/sheet/` so that the two kinds share it.

## Laws a pick must keep (refused by name, never moved)

- The pierce is in the scrap, not on the part that stays.
- The lead room and the kerf compensation hold at the pick.
- The tabs keep their laws (`crates/motion/src/waterjet/tabs.rs`): a pick does not move or remove a tab.

## Done means

- A pin test shows the pierce at the start pick and the jet off at the exit pick, with golden CL.
- A pin test shows a pick whose pierce falls on the part refused by name.
- Undo and redo restore the previous path. MCP `edit_operation` sets the picks.
- Each shipped waterjet golden without a pick is byte-identical.

Safety floor: this changes toolpaths and posted G-code.

Priority note: a follow-up found during work is `P7` by the Issue Law. The other issues of the start and exit series have `P2`. The maintainer decides if this one moves up.
